title: Canonical tensor mate is compatible with etale precomposition
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, let $f:X\to S$ and $h=f\circ u:U\to S$ be compactifiable separated finite-type morphisms between Noetherian schemes (schemes admitting finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings), and let $u:U\to X$ be separated etale of finite type. Work in the entire ordinary derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of constant-$A$ module sheaves, with exact inverse image and derived tensor. Use the compactification-independent projections $P_f,P_h$ and the normalized unbounded compact-support composition comparison, and the right adjunctions $Rf_!\dashv f^\times$, $Rh_!\dashv h^\times$. Put $\omega_f=f^\times A_S$ and $\omega_h=h^\times A_S$. For each $K\in D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ define $\alpha_{f,K}:f^*K\otimes_A^L\omega_f\to f^\times K$ to be the transpose of
$$Rf_!(f^*K\otimes_A^L\omega_f)\xrightarrow{P_f}K\otimes_A^LRf_!\omega_f\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_{f,A_S}}K\otimes_A^LA_S\cong K,$$
and define $\alpha_{h,K}$ in the same way. Let $\lambda_B:u^*f^\times B\xrightarrow{\sim}h^\times B$ be the canonical comparison of right adjoints obtained from the normalized composition $Rf_!Du_!\cong Rh_!$ and the exact sum/evaluation adjunction $Du_!\dashv u^*$. Then
$$\lambda_K\circ u^*\alpha_{f,K}=\alpha_{h,K}\circ(1_{h^*K}\otimes\lambda_{A_S}),$$
where the source is identified with $h^*K\otimes_A^Lu^*\omega_f$ using the canonical inverse-image tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Under this comparison the counit for $h$ is the composite $\epsilon_{f,B}\circ Rf_!(\epsilon_{u,f^\times B})$; all formulas insert the compact-support composition identification. This holds for every unbounded $K$. The notation and functors used here are the ones in [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] [def-kun-derived-tensor] [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] [def-amb-etale-compact-support] [def-asd-compactifiable] [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] [lem-amb-shriek-tensor-composition] [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] [def-weil-etale-morphism] [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring].

proof.text: Write $F=Rf_!$, $E=Du_!$, $V=u^*$, $G=f^\times$ and $H=Rh_!$. Throughout, $\otimes$ means $\otimes_A^L$ and composition is right to left. Write $q_a(K,M):Ra_!(a^*K\otimes M)\to K\otimes Ra_!M$ for the inverse-directed projection denoted $P_a$ in the question. It is a natural isomorphism: choose a compactification $a=rj$, apply the open tensor isomorphism of [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor], and then the proper projection isomorphism of [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection], using the tensor symmetry [lem-kun-tensor-sym] to put $K$ first. The compactification ambient scheme is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since $r$ is proper, hence finite type, over the Noetherian target. These are precisely the factors of the projection used in [lem-amb-shriek-tensor-composition], whose statement includes the refinement compatibility. All these maps exist on the entire unbounded categories.

By [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality] and [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], $E\dashv V$ and $F\dashv G$ are adjunctions on the unbounded categories. Since $U$ and $X$ are Noetherian, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and $u$ is separated of finite type, $u$ has a compactification by [thm-nagata-compactification]. Use [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization] and [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] to fix $c:FE\xrightarrow{\sim}H$: first identify $E$ with compact-support direct image of $u$, then apply the proper/open tower composition. Put $e_C=\epsilon_{u,C}:EVC\to C$. The composite Hom bijection of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] sends $b:M\to VGB$ to $\epsilon_{f,B}\circ F(e_{GB})\circ FE(b)$. On the other hand the specified comparison $\lambda_B$ sends it to $\lambda_B\circ b$, whose $H\dashv h^\times$-transpose, precomposed with $c_M$, is $\epsilon_{h,B}\circ H(\lambda_B\circ b)\circ c_M$. Taking $M=VGB$ and $b=1$ proves
$$\epsilon_{h,B}\circ H(\lambda_B)\circ c_{VGB}=\epsilon_{f,B}\circ F(e_{GB}).$$
This is exactly the claimed composite-counit identity after identifying the right adjoints; it is not a choice of counit on isomorphic functors. Naturality of $c$ then gives the same identity after precomposition by $FE(b)$ for every $b$.

proof.text:
Let $Q(B,M):E(VB\otimes M)\xrightarrow{\sim}B\otimes EM$ be the sum-extension tensor map of [lem-asd-etale-sum-extension-tensor]. Clause (2) of [lem-pur-etale-support-map-compatibility] says that the compactification projection for $u$ becomes the sum-extension projection under its canonical proper-support comparison. Its specified component sends $(s,m)\otimes b$ to $(s,m\otimes s^*b)$; after the tensor symmetries and inversion this is $Q(B,M)$. The proper-support comparison is the same one as [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization]: both send a proper-support section to its sheet components, with inverse given by its graph sections. Thus the inverse-projection identity in [lem-amb-shriek-tensor-composition], for the pair $(u,f)$ (both compactifiable: $f$ by hypothesis, $u$ by [thm-nagata-compactification] as in step 2) and this normalization, gives, for every $M\in D(U_{\mathrm{et}},A)$,
$$q_h(K,M)\circ c_{h^*K\otimes M}=(1_K\otimes c_M)\circ q_f(K,EM)\circ F(Q(f^*K,M)).$$
Here $h^*K=Vf^*K$ by the canonical pullback-composition identification. This equation specifies all occurrences of $c$ below; it is an identity of actual transformations, not just the existence of isomorphic objects.

proof.text:
Put $W=GA_S=\omega_f$, $B=f^*K$, $N=B\otimes W$, and $D=VB\otimes VW$. Let $\theta:D\xrightarrow{\sim}VN$ be the inverse-image tensor comparison; its naturality is part of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Apply the counit identity in [lem-asd-etale-sum-extension-tensor] to $(B,W)$. With $Q=Q(B,VW)$ it says exactly
$$e_N\circ E(\theta)=(1_B\otimes e_W)\circ Q:E(D)\longrightarrow N.$$
In particular this is the fold/evaluation counit, rather than the counit of $u^*\dashv Ru_*$. The coefficient objects $B,W$ are arbitrary complexes, as required by that cited statement.

source.place: Paragraph 3: transpose on U; projection formula followed by the composite etale counit. Explicit agent-written expansion.

proof.text:
Abbreviate $\alpha_{f,K}$ by $a:N\to GK$. By its defining transpose,
$$\epsilon_{f,K}\circ F(a)=(1_K\otimes\epsilon_{f,A_S})\circ q_f(K,W).$$
Using step 2 and naturality of $c$, the $H\dashv h^\times$-transpose of $\lambda_K\circ V(a)\circ\theta:D\to h^\times K$, precomposed with $c_D$, is
$$\epsilon_{f,K}\circ F(e_{GK})\circ FE(V(a))\circ FE(\theta).$$
Naturality of $e$ at $a:N\to GK$ rewrites $e_{GK}\circ EV(a)=a\circ e_N$. Substitute step 4 into this expression. The resulting transpose is
$$\epsilon_{f,K}\circ F(a)\circ F(1_B\otimes e_W)\circ F(Q).$$
These are simply the formula for the Hom bijection, functoriality, and the naturality square for its counit, with all domains fixed in step 4.

source.place: Paragraph 3: transpose on U; projection formula followed by the composite etale counit. Explicit agent-written expansion.

proof.text:
Insert the defining equation for $a$ from step 5. Naturality of the inverse projection $q_f$ at $e_W:EVW\to W$ gives
$$q_f(K,W)\circ F(1_B\otimes e_W)=(1_K\otimes F(e_W))\circ q_f(K,EVW).$$
Bifunctoriality of tensor therefore makes the transpose computed in step 5 equal to
$$(1_K\otimes[\epsilon_{f,A_S}\circ F(e_W)])\circ q_f(K,EVW)\circ F(Q).$$
Finally apply step 3 with $M=VW$ to rewrite this as
$$T=(1_K\otimes[\epsilon_{f,A_S}\circ F(e_W)])\circ(1_K\otimes c_{VW}^{-1})\circ q_h(K,VW)\circ c_D:FE(D)\to K.$$
The projection naturality used here is the naturality of the maps in [lem-amb-shriek-tensor-composition] and of their inverses, not an additional projection formula.

source.place: Paragraph 3: transpose on U; projection formula followed by the composite etale counit. Explicit agent-written expansion.

proof.text:
The other map is $\alpha_{h,K}\circ(1_{h^*K}\otimes\lambda_{A_S}):D\to h^\times K$. Its transpose, by the definition of $\alpha_{h,K}$ and naturality of $q_h$ in the coefficient object, is
$$(1_K\otimes[\epsilon_{h,A_S}\circ H(\lambda_{A_S})])\circ q_h(K,VW).$$
Precompose with $c_D$ and use the counit equation of step 2 at $B=A_S$, namely
$$\epsilon_{h,A_S}\circ H(\lambda_{A_S})=[\epsilon_{f,A_S}\circ F(e_W)]\circ c_{VW}^{-1}.$$
This gives exactly $T$ from step 6. Since $c_D$ is invertible, the two transposes are equal; since the adjunction in [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] is a Hom bijection, the two original maps are equal. Removing $\theta$ by the canonical source identification gives the equality in the statement. Every projection, comparison and adjunction used above was stated on entire ordinary unbounded derived categories over finite $A$, so the calculation applies to every unbounded $K$ without any smoothness, invertibility-of-exponent, constructibility or Tor-amplitude assumption.

lean.note: Returned-head repair: restores the original natural-language statement, including the actual tensor-mate equality and the sum/evaluation counit. The helper is the canonical right mate of etaleAmbientLeftComparison against the degreewise sum adjunction and the exceptional adjunction. The normalized comparison family N has the graph-section and representative characterizations of EtaleCompactSupportNormalization, whose existence is already stated; the assertion holds for every such family. The two alpha maps are written as explicit adjunction transposes, avoiding a duplicate of the downstream smoothTensorDualityMap definition and an import cycle with thm-asd-smooth-tensor. No arbitrary exceptional comparison or extra adjoint-existence hypothesis is imposed.
